one_liner: Dependency scanner that catches supply-chain attacks — install scripts, maintainer changes, typosquats — not just known CVEs.
description: depsentry watches what dependencies do, not just what CVE databases say about them. It flags new install scripts, sudden maintainer handoffs, typosquat-adjacent names, obfuscated payloads, and network calls added in minor versions — the behavioral signals that preceded attacks like event-stream. It runs in CI, comments on the PR that introduces the risk, and scans a 1,200-dependency lockfile in about 40 seconds.
target_user: Security-conscious engineering teams shipping JavaScript and Python

icp.who: Platform and security engineers at companies with large npm or PyPI dependency trees
icp.pain: CVE scanners only alert after disclosure, which is weeks too late for supply-chain attacks that live in install scripts and hijacked maintainer accounts
icp.buying_trigger: A supply-chain incident in the news that maps uncomfortably well onto the team's own dependency tree

differentiators: Behavioral analysis of packages: install scripts, maintainer changes, added network calls — signals CVE scanners don't model
Retro-test shows it would have flagged the event-stream attack 11 days before public disclosure
PR-level comments on the exact change that introduces risk, not a weekly digest of noise
proof_points: Retro-analysis: flags the event-stream/flatmap-stream attack 11 days before disclosure
Scans a 1,200-dependency lockfile in 40 seconds in CI
Free for open-source repositories, already running on 300 public projects
pricing_current: free for open source; team plan $199/month

voice.sample_phrase: CVE feeds tell you about last month's attack. We watch what your dependencies do today.

signals: Free OSS tier live with public installs
Team pricing published but onboarding is white-glove

gaps: Python coverage newer than npm coverage
No public detection-rate benchmark against Socket

confidence.notes: The retro-test claim is specific and falsifiable. Detection quality relative to competitors is not yet independently measured.
